A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BracketIRE/BracketIRE+ study. Their methods, equations, experiments, figures, tables, and supplementary material are readable and can be matched despite the changed title and formatting.

before.justification: Sections 5–6 and the supplementary material report original synthetic and real-image evaluations, component ablations, and computational measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark and ablation results and reports additional EMA-removal and loss-weight experiments in supplementary Tables E–G.

M1.justification: Section 3.1 changes the specified gamma exponent from 2.2 to 1/2.2. Equation (7) and Figure 1 remove the direct previous-state input to the frame-specific block, leaving that input in the common block. The overall TMRNet framework and three adaptation losses remain.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same HDR-video-derived synthetic data and Xiaomi 10S nighttime dataset for BracketIRE and BracketIRE+, including 4× super-resolution. The additional adaptation analyses introduce no new dataset, task, sensor, or evaluated domain.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains DBSR, MFIR, BIPNet, Burstormer, RBSR, AHDRNet, HDRGAN, HDR-Tran., SCTNet, and Kim et al. The full computational comparison in supplementary Table A also retains its comparator set; v2's main-text timing table redisplays a subset.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 changes the reported synthetic training budget from 300 to 400 epochs and the final learning rate from 1e-5 to 1e-6. Input gamma preprocessing is also revised, and new adaptation experiments introduce EMA-removal and loss-weight controls. The PDFs do not establish whether existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Supplementary Section E adds an EMA-removal control, sensitivity tests for lambda_self and lambda_neg, and further visual loss ablations in Figure A. Table E removes the BracketIRE+ ablation column. The existing burst, frame-count, exposure-combination, and network-depth analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. v2 adds no statistical uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: All Table 2 benchmark values remain identical. New results include NaN without EMA, CLIP-IQA/MUSIQ of 0.2279/27.899 at lambda_self=0.5, and 0.2255/28.051 at lambda_neg=0.3. BracketIRE+ loss-ablation entries are removed from Table E, and qualitative example panels are replaced or expanded.

T1.justification: Equation (7) substantively revises the formal recurrence: H_i = A_i^s(G_i, H_{i-1}) becomes H_i = A_i^s(G_i). The image-formation model, noise assumptions, and adaptation-loss definitions otherwise remain unchanged; no new theorems or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims: unifying restoration and enhancement through exposure bracketing, proposing TMRNet and self-supervised adaptation, providing datasets, and outperforming competing multi-image methods. The revised title preserves this scope.

C2.justification: v2 adds a diminishing-returns rationale for the negative loss and qualifies no-reference metrics as unstable auxiliary evidence. New supplementary Section G states that differing sensor characteristics require tailored training and limit cross-sensor generalization.

D1.justification: Section 5.2 explicitly clarifies that baselines are deployed directly on real images while TMRNet receives adaptation; Section 6.1 identifies the simulator used for burst controls. Hyperparameter descriptions are revised. Hardware, supplementary noise-generation details, and code/data/model access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 107 cited works and substantive research positioning are retained. Reference renumbering and SelfHDR's update from an arXiv citation to ICLR 2024 are bibliographic changes.

P1.justification: The title is revised, passages in the introduction and method are edited, and adaptation and simulation explanations are expanded. An inference-time subsection and supplementary applications/limitations section are added, while the overall section order and narrative remain stable.

P2.justification: The document changes throughout from two-column to single-column presentation, with resized and rearranged displays. Figures 1–3 are redrawn or reorganized, qualitative panels are reselected, Table E is restructured, and Tables F–G and an additional visual-ablation figure are added. Existing appendix timings also receive a main-text table.

improvement.justification: The added EMA-removal and loss-weight checks strengthen the adaptation analysis, while explicit sensor and metric limitations improve transparency. These provide a modest net gain despite the loss of BracketIRE+ ablation detail. Revised training settings accompanying unchanged benchmark scores remain unexplained, limiting the improvement in experimental clarity.
